newsitem.title: UK: LVMH mulls legal action on Guinness merger - paper.
newsitem.headline: LVMH mulls legal action on Guinness merger - paper.

text.p: LVMH, aiming to block the Guinness Grand Metropolitan merger, has begun moves that could lead to legal action against the British companies, the Sunday Times reported.

LVMH chairman Bernard Arnault has written to his Guinness and Grand Met counterparts Tony Greener and George Bull seeking assurances that confidential arrangements relating to LVMH's business has not passed between the two sides, the report said.
French drinks and luxury goods company LVMH, Guinness' biggest shareholder with a 14 percent stake, opposes the planned merger.
LVMH has a number of joint ventures with Guinness to distribute drinks in France, the United States and the Far East.
The report said Arnault was expected to seek legal redress unless he received the assurances he was seeking.
Quoting London-based lawyers, it said he could sue for damages or seek an injunction preventing Guinness from using information relating to the joint ventures.
An injunction would provide a hurdle to the planned merger as the distribution networks are commercially significant, especially those in Asia, the report said.
